title: Dogs helping stressed out students
paragraphs: Some people say that dogs are man’s best friend – good companions, loyal and loveable. Of course, they can be more than just a pet as certain breeds are excellent working dogs too. We know about the amazing help guide dogs give to blind people and, more recently, a new role has been found for the animals – working as therapy dogs in universities.

Research by Washington State University in the US, has found spending time with a pooch can help stressed out students. Patricia Pendry from the university told the BBC that a study of 300 undergraduates had found weekly hour-long sessions with dogs brought to the university by professional handlers had made stressed students at "high risk of academic failure" or dropping out, "feel relaxed and accepted". The dogs helped them to concentrate, learn and remember information.

I know that stroking a dog helps me to relax; other research has shown that petting animals can reduce stress hormone levels and anxiety, so it makes sense to introduce them into an environment where people are stressed. The BBC’s education correspondent Sean Coughlan writes that around 1,000 campuses in the US already use therapy pets and it’s becoming more common in the UK. For example, The University of Middlesex has employed ‘canine teaching assistants’ to help stop lonely students dropping out. Fiona Suthers, head of clinical skills at the university, says that five Labradors had a “stringent assessment” to ensure they had the right temperament. But she adds “it’s hard to describe the impact of just having a dog lying down in the corner of a class.”

Using dogs for therapy can also help the dogs themselves. In Wales, Swansea University Students’ Union has used rescued greyhounds to help students unwind between exams. Sessions allow mistreated and abandoned dogs to interact with humans and begin to trust them again. Student Union education officer Chloe Hutchinson told the BBC that “a lot of students have dogs at home and might be a bit homesick, especially around exam time when it is stressful and you just want your home comforts.” So if you’re a student who’s been working like a dog, but you still feel like you haven’t a dog’s chance in passing your exams, maybe introducing a four-legged friend into your life might be the help you need.

vocabulary.example: Dogs are faithful companions to humans.
vocabulary.translation: 狗是人类忠实的伙伴。

vocabulary.entry: loyal /ˈlɔɪəl/ adj. 忠诚的；忠心的
vocabulary.example: She has always been loyal to her friends.
vocabulary.translation: 她对朋友一直很忠诚。

vocabulary.example: Golden retrievers are a popular breed of dog.
vocabulary.translation: 金毛寻回犬是一种很受欢迎的犬种。

vocabulary.example: Shepherds use working dogs to help manage sheep.
vocabulary.translation: 牧羊人用工作犬帮忙看管羊群。

vocabulary.example: The guide dog led its owner safely across the street.
vocabulary.translation: 导盲犬领着主人安全地穿过了马路。

vocabulary.example: The therapy dog visits the hospital every week to cheer up patients.
vocabulary.translation: 这只治疗犬每周都会去医院，为病人带去欢乐。

vocabulary.example: Our neighbor has a cute little pooch.
vocabulary.translation: 我们邻居家有一只可爱的小狗。

vocabulary.example: He is an undergraduate studying physics at Oxford University.
vocabulary.translation: 他是牛津大学物理系的一名本科生。

vocabulary.entry: handler /ˈhændlə(r)/ n. 驯兽师；管理者
vocabulary.example: The dog and its handler won first prize in the competition.
vocabulary.translation: 这只狗和它的驯兽师在比赛中获得了一等奖。

vocabulary.entry: academic failure /ˌækəˈdemɪk ˈfeɪljə(r)/ 学业失败
vocabulary.example: Poor attendance can lead to academic failure for some students.
vocabulary.translation: 出勤不佳可能会导致一些学生学业失败。

vocabulary.entry: concentrate /ˈkɒnsntreɪt/ v. 集中注意力；专注
vocabulary.example: I find it hard to concentrate when it's noisy.
vocabulary.translation: 环境嘈杂的时候，我很难集中注意力。

vocabulary.example: She gently stroked the cat's fur.
vocabulary.translation: 她轻轻地抚摸着猫咪的毛。

vocabulary.example: Talking to a friend can help reduce anxiety.
vocabulary.translation: 和朋友聊聊天有助于缓解焦虑。

vocabulary.example: The library is the most popular place on campus.
vocabulary.translation: 图书馆是校园里最受欢迎的地方。

vocabulary.example: The center provides training for canine assistants.
vocabulary.translation: 该中心为犬类助理提供培训。

vocabulary.entry: stringent /ˈstrɪndʒənt/ adj. 严格的；严厉的
vocabulary.example: The company has stringent safety rules for employees.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司对员工有严格的安全规定。

vocabulary.example: The dog has a calm and gentle temperament.
vocabulary.translation: 这只狗性情平和温顺。

vocabulary.entry: rescued /ˈreskjuːd/ adj. 获救的；被营救的
vocabulary.example: The animal shelter is home to many rescued cats and dogs.
vocabulary.translation: 这家动物收容所是许多获救猫狗的家。

vocabulary.example: Greyhounds are known for their speed and agility.
vocabulary.translation: 灵缇犬以速度和敏捷著称。

vocabulary.example: I like to unwind by listening to music after work.
vocabulary.translation: 下班后我喜欢听音乐放松。

vocabulary.entry: work like a dog /wɜːk laɪk ə dɒɡ/ 拼命工作；苦干
vocabulary.example: He worked like a dog to finish the project on time.
vocabulary.translation: 他拼命工作，为的是按时完成这个项目。

vocabulary.entry: not have a dog’s chance /nɒt hæv ə dɒɡz tʃɑːns/ 毫无机会；没有可能
vocabulary.example: You don't have a dog’s chance of winning the race without training.
vocabulary.translation: 不经过训练，你毫无可能赢得这场比赛。

sentences.english: Some people say that dogs are man’s best friend – good companions, loyal and loveable.
sentences.chinese: 有人说，狗是人类最好的朋友——它们是贴心的伙伴，忠诚又惹人喜爱。

sentences.english: Of course, they can be more than just a pet as certain breeds are excellent working dogs too.
sentences.chinese: 当然，狗的作用远不止是宠物，有些品种还是出色的工作犬。

sentences.english: We know about the amazing help guide dogs give to blind people and, more recently, a new role has been found for the animals – working as therapy dogs in universities.
sentences.chinese: 我们都知道导盲犬能为盲人提供极大的帮助，而近来，人们又为狗狗们找到了一个新角色——在大学里担任治疗犬。

sentences.english: Research by Washington State University in the US, has found spending time with a pooch can help stressed out students.
sentences.chinese: 美国华盛顿州立大学的一项研究发现，和狗狗相处能帮助压力山大的学生缓解焦虑。

sentences.english: Patricia Pendry from the university told the BBC that a study of 300 undergraduates had found weekly hour-long sessions with dogs brought to the university by professional handlers had made stressed students at "high risk of academic failure" or dropping out, "feel relaxed and accepted".
sentences.chinese: 该校的帕特里夏·彭德里向英国广播公司表示，一项针对300名本科生的研究显示，由专业驯养员带进校园的狗狗，每周和学生进行一次时长一小时的互动，可以让那些“面临高危辍学压力风险”的学生“感到放松和被接纳”。

sentences.english: The dogs helped them to concentrate, learn and remember information.
sentences.chinese: 狗狗还能帮助他们集中注意力，更好地学习和记忆知识。

sentences.english: I know that stroking a dog helps me to relax; other research has shown that petting animals can reduce stress hormone levels and anxiety, so it makes sense to introduce them into an environment where people are stressed.
sentences.chinese: 我知道撸狗能帮我放松；其他研究也表明，抚摸动物可以降低压力激素水平，缓解焦虑情绪。因此，把它们引入压力环境是合理的做法。

sentences.english: The BBC’s education correspondent Sean Coughlan writes that around 1,000 campuses in the US already use therapy pets and it’s becoming more common in the UK.
sentences.chinese: 英国广播公司教育记者肖恩·考夫兰写道，美国已有约1000所大学校园配备了治疗宠物，这种做法在英国也正变得越来越普遍。

sentences.english: For example, The University of Middlesex has employed ‘canine teaching assistants’ to help stop lonely students dropping out.
sentences.chinese: 例如，密德萨斯大学就聘请了“犬类教学助理”，帮助孤独的学生避免辍学。

sentences.english: Fiona Suthers, head of clinical skills at the university, says that five Labradors had a “stringent assessment” to ensure they had the right temperament.
sentences.chinese: 该校临床技能负责人菲奥娜·萨瑟斯表示，五只拉布拉多犬都经过了“严格的评估”，以确保它们拥有合适的性情。

sentences.english: But she adds “it’s hard to describe the impact of just having a dog lying down in the corner of a class.”
sentences.chinese: 但她补充道：“仅仅让一只狗趴在教室角落能产生多大的影响，这还很难说。”

sentences.english: Using dogs for therapy can also help the dogs themselves.
sentences.chinese: 让狗狗参与治疗工作，对它们自身也有好处。

sentences.english: In Wales, Swansea University Students’ Union has used rescued greyhounds to help students unwind between exams.
sentences.chinese: 在威尔士，斯旺西大学学生会就利用获救的灵缇犬，帮助学生在考试间隙放松身心。

sentences.english: Sessions allow mistreated and abandoned dogs to interact with humans and begin to trust them again.
sentences.chinese: 这些互动环节能让受过虐待和被遗弃的狗狗与人类交流，重新建立对人类的信任。

sentences.english: Student Union education officer Chloe Hutchinson told the BBC that “a lot of students have dogs at home and might be a bit homesick, especially around exam time when it is stressful and you just want your home comforts.”
sentences.chinese: 学生会教育干事克洛伊·哈钦森向英国广播公司表示：“很多学生家里都养狗，他们可能会有点想家，尤其是在考试期间，压力很大，就格外想念家里的温馨时光。”

sentences.english: So if you’re a student who’s been working like a dog, but you still feel like you haven’t a dog’s chance in passing your exams, maybe introducing a four-legged friend into your life might be the help you need.
sentences.chinese: 所以，如果你是一名学生，已经拼命用功，却仍觉得考试及格无望，或许让一位四条腿的朋友走进你的生活，就是你需要的助力。
